newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Bouygues Abidjan bridge deal likely soon.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues Abidjan bridge deal likely soon.

text.p: A contract to build a toll bridge across the lagoon in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's commercial capital, is likely to go to Bouygues-SETAO, part of France's Bouygues on July 31, the government said on Thursday.

An upturn in the economy of the world's biggest cocoa producer has brought with it an influx of new and second-hand cars resulting in serious rush hour bottle-necks on the two bridges currently linking different parts of the city.

"Talks are currently continuing on points relating to the timetable of the work...after the signing of an agreement, which could come on July 31," the minutes of Wednesday's cabinet meeting in the government daily, Fraternite-Matin, said.
The bridge would link the residential Riviera district with Marcory, a mixed residential and industrial area.

According to the timetable laid out in the minutes, work on the site could begin in January 1998, with work on the bridge itself starting in March. No completion date was given and there were no details immediately available on the value of the contract.
Drivers will have to pay a toll to use the new bridge. The state will own a maximum 20 percent of the operating company, according to the minutes.
